summary.intent: Plan, verify, execute, and ship phase 64 (Rotation Soundness — Revocation Guarantees) of CipherBox, which fills four throwing seams in the rotation engine and fixes three critical bugs (D-02 re-seal, D-06 node-identity, D-07 ordering).
summary.outcome: All 8 plans across 6 waves were executed and verified (297 unit tests passing, 3/3 e2e tests passing on the live stack), with two findings deferred as todos; /ship-phase 64 was queued after the user chose to ship-as-is.

repo: The GSD plan-checker enforces that RESEARCH.md 'Open Questions' must be marked '(RESOLVED)' and VALIDATION.md per-task map must not be TBD before execution can proceed.
tsup (esbuild bundler) does not type-check — only explicit `tsc --noEmit` catches type errors in source; test files are excluded from tsconfig.build.json so test-file type errors are invisible to CI.
Pre-existing type debt exists in cas.test.ts and grant.test.ts (vi.fn two-type-arg syntax); these are invisible to CI and out of scope for phase 64.
The gsd-tools commit helper reliably returns 'commit_failed' even on successful commits (known false-negative documented in project memory); verify via `git log` instead.

The rotation engine design (§4.5) explicitly endorses double-rotation as the crash-recovery model — a fresh full rotateOne is the recovery path, not a no-double-bump guard; SC#4's 'without double-bumping' wording contradicts this.
lint-staged git stash-pop can conflict and dump untracked files from unrelated old stashes into the working tree when a background git operation races with a commit.

code.finding: D-02 bug: sealChildReadKey sealed under the child's own pre-rotation key (parameter minamed 'parentReadKey'); the re-seal must happen out-of-band in the BFS caller under the parent's NEW readKey' and be written back to parent's SealedChildRef.

D-01 fail-closed guard: `if (!nodeIpnsPrivateKey) { throw ... }` enforces that IPNS publish key must come from nodeKeySource. The remaining PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY at L394 is the write-body seal key (role 0x04), legitimately deferred to Phase 65.

D-07 ordering bugs: completedNodeIds.add fires before reMintGrantsRootedAt (should be after); resume guard at L458-462 short-circuits without calling verifySubtreeClean (should rebuild frontier from published IPNS truth).

verifySubtreeClean is only invoked when completedNodeIds is non-empty; a true fresh-record resume (empty completedNodeIds, D-03 model) skips it and re-enters rotateOne(root) causing AEAD failure under the old root key. Root has no parent mirror so the convergence-skip guard at L878 cannot cover it.

D-02 fix location: the out-of-band sealChildReadKey call in the BFS caller writes updatedChildReadKeySealed back onto parent's SealedChildRef[N].readKeySealed — this is the correct location, not inside rotateOne.

The per-node convergence-skip guard only covers frontier children via parent mirror; the root node has no parent mirror and cannot be skipped, making fresh-record resume require Phase 68 durable key floor.
Stale doc comment 'mark contentRekeyPending' remains; contentRekeyPending is Phase 65 scope (node/v3 schema frozen this phase).

Phase-64-introduced @ts-expect-error directives were placed above `await expect(` (L83) instead of directly above the erroring updateFolderMetadataAndPublish call (L84), making them 'unused' while the real TS2345 fired below.

New test file imported CryptoError from '@cipherbox/core' but it is only exported from '@cipherbox/crypto'; runtime passed only because toThrow(undefined) matches any throw, masking the wrong package reference.

D-06 bug: `id: params.nodeId ?? crypto.randomUUID()` and `generation: params.nodeGeneration ?? 0` silently break AAD stability and convergence tests at all 6 updateFolderMetadataAndPublish call sites in client.ts that omit nodeId/nodeGeneration.

workflow: Always run `tsc --noEmit` explicitly after executor subagents complete — tsup build success does not imply type correctness.
When running background git operations (1Password SSH signing), never overlap them with other git operations; the 'could not write index' error is a transient lock race, not a permanent failure.

After a lint-staged stash-pop conflict, verify the working tree before retrying: check for stash-origin untracked dirs, restore HEAD version of conflicted files, move untracked stash garbage aside before re-committing.

For plan-checker findings: doc-resolution blockers (RESEARCH.md markers, VALIDATION.md status) can be fixed by the orchestrator directly; substantive plan content gaps should be sent to the planner via SendMessage to retain deep plan context.
The GSD executor's `commit_failed` JSON return is a reliable false-negative; always verify via `git log --oneline -1` rather than trusting the helper's return value.
Run the full package test suite (not just the plan's target files) after any plan that touches shared infrastructure files like cas.ts — widening a type union can silently break consumers.

friction: lint-staged stash-pop conflict mid-session: a background git commit raced with a foreground commit, causing a stash-pop that dumped untracked files from an unrelated old stash (phase-3 WIP) into the working tree, requiring manual recovery.

VALIDATION.md was written as a skeleton (TBD per-task map) per the workflow spec, but the plan-checker flagged it as a warning requiring full population before execution — the workflow spec and checker behavior were misaligned.

SC#4 ('abort and resume without double-bumping') in the ROADMAP directly contradicted the design document (§4.5 explicitly endorses double-rotation as recovery), only discovered during e2e gate review.
The 64-08 e2e suite had to be written around Phase-68-scope limitations (seeding completedNodeIds instead of truly fresh record), obscuring the real engine gap until post-execution review.
tsup builds succeed even when there are type errors in test files — the wave-1 typecheck gap was only discovered by running explicit `tsc --noEmit`, not caught by the executor's default build step.
The GSD commit helper consistently returns 'commit_failed' JSON even on successful commits, requiring an extra git log verification step after every commit.
open_items: Phase 68: implement durable job-record floor so crash-resume works from a truly fresh RotationJobRecord (empty completedNodeIds) without needing the pre-seeded completedNodeIds workaround.

Fix HIGH-4 merge bug: mergeConcurrentChildren uses 'remote wins' merge policy which downgrades an already-rotated child's readKeySealed on a CAS-409 concurrent-add; correct policy is local-wins + add remote-only children.
Phase 65: wire contentRekeyPending marker and write-body keys (PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY at engine.ts L394 remains as a known placeholder).

Pre-existing type errors in cas.test.ts (from #494) and grant.test.ts (from Phase 63) use the old vi.fn<[A], B>() two-type-arg syntax; invisible to CI because test files are excluded from tsconfig.build.json.
Stale 'mark contentRekeyPending' doc comment at engine.ts L194 should be removed or updated to reference Phase 65.
SC#4 wording in the ROADMAP ('without double-bumping') should be corrected to match the design's actual crash-recovery model (double-rotation is safe and intended per §4.5).
